recommendation: Choose Option 3(a) and Option 3(b), then Option 1. The Gate-2 ruling may be one shared D-000 entry for DR-131, DR-133, and DR-117 only if it states a common interpretation and separately measures each row. It must not say that D-249 through D-253 silently superseded D-154. Obtain a fresh application-grade dual review of the final DR-131 contract bytes before the DR-131 opening entry. Under the conservative D-056 reading, author the G24 through G28 fixture implementations before the later, separate DR-131 SATISFIED-GRADE cycle.
rationale: The existing v2 verdicts are genuine dual ACCEPT at zero blockers and zero SHOULD-FIX, but their own grade text is candidate-only; D-001 requires the independent review itself to grant application-grade acceptance, so a fresh neutral review is the clean Gate-1 route. Claude is also right that opening and SATISFIED-GRADE must remain distinct acts. Its Gate-2 rationale is too categorical, however. D-154 expressly found DR-131 Gates 2 and 3 to hold, while the later G24-G28 joins place fixture-authoring leftovers on the gate rows and preserve the DR-131 NT closures. D-015/D-085 and D-207 show that row acceptance remainder and gate-side authoring have been treated as distinct layers. A shared ruling is still useful to make that reading explicit, and sequencing fixtures before SATISFIED-GRADE is conservative and compatible with D-056. D-000 permits one reviewed rule-governed entry to cover multiple applications if every decision, alternative, rationale, review, and reversibility term is documented; D-056's row-specific requirement attaches to the later SATISFIED-GRADE review, not to the antecedent interpretive ruling.

refutations.claim: The live DR-131 row records preview-analyze-contract.v2 only as a non-applied candidate and leaves the row OPEN.
refutations.evidence: File 08 DR-131 names digest 081ff7fb529b34a3db3ac9f4c7505848e2253be12b5a867d39b49b3a26d56970 and says CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, and Not SATISFIED; D-138 and D-141 say Class A is not opened.

refutations.claim: The existing independent verdicts do not grant application-grade acceptance.
refutations.evidence: The Claude verdict accepts an independently reviewed DR-131 design-contract candidate and says it opens no Class A; the Codex verdict limits itself to evidence on the candidate bytes and sets opensD056ClassA and appliesOrSealsCandidate to false. D-001 says zero blockers alone is insufficient.

refutations.claim: A fresh application-grade review is the least exposed way to establish D-056 Gate 1.
refutations.evidence: D-001 T2-02 requires the independent review to grant application-grade acceptance with no candidate-only limitation. D-015 measured that property in the verdict before D-085 relied on it; neither D-138 nor the v2 verdicts made that measurement.

refutations.claim: D-154 and D-249 through D-253 are necessarily contradictory findings about DR-131 Gate 2.
refutations.evidence: D-154 says Gates 2 and 3 hold for DR-131's eight NT classes. The current G24-G28 joins put only their gate-specific FX-AUTHORING obligation in summary.leftoverDesign while keeping the NT unnamed-remainder-closed obligations in specifiedNotLeftover; D-249 through D-253 record those gate joins without reopening DR-131's NT classes.

refutations.claim: D-056 treats fixture authoring as design work that cannot be split as a row's execution-only remainder.
refutations.evidence: D-056 Gate 2 excludes authoring of fixtures, schemas, successors, actor-joins, missing design, and undecided numbers, and Decision clause 5 says fixture and harness-specification authoring remains design work.

refutations.claim: The precedents establish that every gate-side fixture-authoring leftover automatically reopens the riding architecture row's Gate 2.
refutations.evidence: D-085 records DR-102 SATISFIED with CC execution left at G21, while later G21 bytes still carry fixture authoring. More directly, D-207 says DR-117 Gates 2 and 3 continue to hold while separately preserving G29/G30 fixture-authoring leftovers. The record therefore distinguishes the layers rather than stating the claimed automatic rule.

refutations.claim: The later fixture-authoring work can nevertheless be sequenced before SATISFIED-GRADE without violating D-056.
refutations.evidence: D-056 expressly allows fixture and harness-specification authoring as lawful design work before the later per-row SATISFIED-GRADE cycle; the G24-G28 joins identify the outstanding authoring and say execution remains qualification.

refutations.claim: One Gate-2 ruling covering all three rows is unlawful under D-000.
refutations.evidence: D-000 requires adversarial review and complete documentation but contains no one-row-per-entry rule. COORD includes general multi-row rules such as D-056 and multi-subject acts such as D-132. A shared entry is lawful if it records separate row findings; D-056 still requires the later SATISFIED-GRADE review of 'that row'.

refutations.claim: The candidate's DR-117 join still pins preview-product-boundary-successor.v5 rather than the D-207 v8 remasurement.
refutations.evidence: preview-analyze-contract.v2 joins.dr117 names preview-product-boundary-successor.v5 at 5face6a97b311117569044c0214452571e6d3f051e1ab9b38f46abf442ce1262; D-207 records preview-product-boundary-successor.v8.

refutations.claim: The Class A opening has no value other than unlocking SATISFIED-GRADE.
refutations.evidence: An opening entry also resolves the independently disputed T2-02 application-grade property and records the owner-controlled product-contract disposition. Its lack of an immediate SATISFIED edit does not make that legal effect valueless.

amendments: Frame the shared Gate-2 act as a common rule plus three separately evidenced applications; state whether it interprets D-056 or is a scoped successor amendment.
Do not describe the G24-G28 gate-authoring flags as silently overturning D-154; reconcile the row/gate distinction expressly.
Ensure the fresh application-grade verdict pair reviews the exact final contract bytes cited by the opening entry.
Keep fixture authoring before SATISFIED-GRADE as conservative sequencing, not as a precedent-proven automatic reopening of DR-131 Gate 2.
